title: Kirmington — 166 Squadron Memorial Garden
memorial_address: Main Street, Kirmington, North Lincolnshire DN39 6YW
inscription:
YE THAT LIVE ON MID ENGLAND'S PASTURES GREEN
THINK ON US AND WHAT MIGHT HAVE BEEN
THIS MEMORIAL IS DEDICATED TO ALL THE MEN AND WOMEN WHO SERVED WITH 166 SQUADRON
AT ROYAL AIR FORCE KIRMINGTON 1943-1945
OF WHOM 921 GAVE THEIR LIVES THAT WE MIGHT BE FREE
crew_summary: 921 aircrew killed serving with 166 Squadron at RAF Kirmington 1943-1945
narrative: 166 Squadron flew Lancaster bombers from RAF Kirmington in North Lincolnshire from January 1943 to the end of the war. In that time, the squadron flew 5,061 sorties, lost 178 aircraft, and saw 921 of its airmen killed — one of the heaviest toll figures in Bomber Command. It stands as the primary commemorative site for one of the most active and costly Lancaster squadrons of the strategic bombing campaign. The stone of remembrance, mounted with a Lancaster propeller blade on a plinth, and surrounded by three flagpoles and memorial benches, provides a tangible focus for remembrance in the community that lived beside the airfield.
memorial_details:
Stone of Remembrance with a Lancaster propeller blade mounted on a plinth. Three flagpoles. Black marble tablet commemorating the 70th anniversary of Operation Manna. Two memorial benches. Primary squadron memorial for 166 Squadron RAF. Located in the village centre, accessible year-round. IWM War Memorials Register reference: IWM 51736.

The Memorial Garden in the centre of Kirmington village was established by the 166 Squadron Association and dedicated in September 1988.

A black marble tablet marks the 70th anniversary of Operation Manna — the food-drop mission to occupied Holland in April-May 1945 — in which 166 Squadron participated.
